My ex was initially diagnosed Bi-Polar, then that was changed to Borderline Personality Disorder, but she decided she didn't really need medication, a bunch of her idiot friends somehow convinced her that a gluten free diet and going vegan would solve all her problems. It didn't. If anything it just gave her something else to obsess over (her diet).

Dealing with someone who is mentally ill is incredibly difficult, it's exhausting and demoralizing, reason and common sense don't work because they don't think the same way you do. Mentally ill people are literally living in a different version of reality.

My best advice would be, don't do this on your own. You need help.

If you try to push her to get medical help, and no-one else is involved, she can dismiss your opinion, she may even decide you're out to get her, that you hate her (see: mentally ill). If that happens she may become aggressive or violent towards you. (I would honestly advise you to find a voice recording app or similar for your phone, if things get unpleasant and someone calls the cops, they'll arrest you because your a guy, a recording of events my be the only thing that saves you.)

If she has family that she's in regular contact with, and gets on with, you should approach them first. Preferably her mother, maybe an older sister, maybe her father, or possibly a close female friend. Talk to her family and tell them that you're concerned, tell them about the earlier diagnosis, tell them about common symptoms of bi-polar, tell them about her current behavior, tell them that you don't know what to do and that you need help. Tell them that you just want her to see a doctor, but you don't know how to approach her about it, and you're worried that it will damage your marriage if you do. I know you're tired, exhausted from dealing with it, but don't tell them about how it's affecting you. This is about your wife.

With any luck, they'll start observing her behavior, and recognizing the bi-polar symptoms in her behavior. Hopefully they'll start hinting that she should get help. If you're really lucky they'll take her under their wing and go see a doctor with her. Then all you have do is support her and help her along the path to recovery. When it's a team effort the burden is slightly lighter.

My ex was off and on her medication every few weeks/months. One week she'd be sure she didn't need her medication because she'd been 'eating healthy for ages', next week she'd be out drinking and taking drugs like it was New Years, then she'd feel terrible so she'd go through her 'detox' phase, and back to eating gluten free and vegan and still feeling like shit. Then she'd eventually realize she needed to be back on her medication to feel well again. So she'd go back on her medication and she'd finally start feeling well again. After that she'd decide she didn't need her medication because she didn't like some of the side effects, and she'd been 'eating healthy for ages'. Rinse and repeat.

She was normal, and pleasant to be around maybe 2 weeks in every 8. But 2 of those 8 weeks were absolute hell. Eventually after nearly a year and a half, she came to me during her cleansing/detox phase, when she was obsessing over gluten free vegan food, and drinking only water. She told me that she couldn't be with someone who ate hamburgers or drank coffee, and if I didn't become a gluten free vegan she couldn't be with me anymore. I still feel kinda bad, but I saw my 'Out' and I took it. I put on my best sad face, gathered up my things and walked away. It's possibly the most relief I've ever felt in my life.

The thing with mental illnesses is that most of them can't be 'cured', they can only be treated. Sometimes they get better over time, sometimes their illness just becomes 'the way things are' for the rest of their lives. And some people with mental illness just don't want to be treated.

If she doesn't want help, your life will become nothing but looking after her, dealing with her shit, it's like being in an abusive relationship. There's no shame in walking away. At least you can say you tried.
